read.thesis: Wholesale-led AUM growth with SME retail still in consolidation; Q2 disbursement record Rs 385 crore but gross NPS rose to 1.13% from 0.51% a year ago, against a prior "no absolute increase in NPA" guidance.

summary.headline: CSL Finance Q2 FY27 AUM rose 16% YoY to Rs 1,627 crore on record Rs 385 crore disbursement, with wholesale driving growth and SME retail still consolidating.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 saw record quarterly disbursement of Rs 385 crore (up 31% YoY, 20% QoQ) and AUM of Rs 1,627 crore (up 16% YoY, 7% QoQ on-book growth). Wholesale drove growth while SME retail remained in a consolidation phase with tighter credit policy and branch rationalisation. Profitability improved: NII and PBT both grew 21% YoY, and annualised ROE rose to 14.86%. Gross NPS rose to 1.13% from 0.95% in Q1, a sign of asset quality pressure, mainly in the SME book.

segments.name: Wholesale (builder/project lending)
segments.commentary: Primary driver of AUM growth; 128 active projects funded across roughly 80-90 builders, with a pipeline of about Rs 300-400 crore under due diligence or sanction at end-September. Management says 30-40% of the portfolio is affordable housing and 35% small housing, with the remaining ~30% exposed to slower-selling projects.

segments.name: SME Retail (LAP/LAF)
segments.commentary: In consolidation: disbursements higher QoQ but measured. Gross NPAs on the SME book were about Rs 17 crore on roughly Rs 450 crore (around 3% per analyst's calculation). Management stopped ticket sizes above Rs 50 lakh about 18 months ago and is de-emphasising sub-Rs 10 lakh loans; 35 branches across 7 states, with non-performing branches being rationalised or relocated.

guidance_outlook: Wholesale expected to remain the main AUM growth engine for the rest of FY27, funded by undrawn limits of Rs 210 crore.
SME retail disbursements expected to improve in H2 FY27 as consolidation takes hold; management said the last two months were the best of the year for SME and expects better numbers after Diwali.
Joint lending (off-book) expected to build up over coming quarters to add fee income.
No new product verticals (gold loans, two-wheelers) planned for the next 15-18 months; focus stays on SME LAF.
Management prioritises asset quality and conservative leverage over growth; a new full-time SME CEO is in place, with a fuller review promised next quarter.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 35 branches across 7 states; ongoing rationalisation of non-performing branches and relocation of sub-scale branches (Gujarat, Rajasthan rural).
Lender base of 35 across PSBs, private banks, SFCs and NBFCs.
Funding headroom: Rs 210 crore undrawn limits plus Rs 76.8 crore liquidity; ALM positive in all buckets; credit rating A-table (Acuity Rating & Research).
demand_pricing: Analyst asked about a possible slowdown in residential real estate; management says affordable housing (30-40% of wholesale book) sells out via lottery on launch day, and small plotted housing (35%) shows no slowdown.
Management cites a challenged subset of roughly 30% of the wholesale book where sales could be slower; it says it avoids new geographies lacking infrastructure.
SME competition is high in smaller tickets; over-leveraged MSME borrowers and stagnant income growth have not eased, per management.
Joint lending with industry partners is used to participate in larger transactions and earn fee income.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the wholesale approval and disbursement pipeline, and what is the outlook for residential real estate slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipeline of about Rs 300-400 crore at end-September, with due diligence and some sanctions done. Management says it lends against project cash flows with escrow control and focuses on affordable and small housing, where it sees no sales slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Clarify the count of wholesale active accounts: are the 128 accounts projects or builders?
qa_highlights.answer: 128 are projects, not builders. Around 80-90 builders are behind them, and some builders have 2-3 projects, with exposure limits set for larger borrowers.

qa_highlights.question: SME gross NPA is about 3% on roughly Rs 450 crore. What is the outlook and strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the NPAs mostly come from accounts above Rs 50 lakh, stopped about 18 months ago; no new NPAs have come in the last 18 months. Focus shifts to Rs 10-50 lakh SARFAESI-compliant loans, with a new full-time CEO overseeing SME and distribution as the next priority.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add new products such as gold loans or two-wheeler loans over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management sees no new product for the next 15-18 months, citing scope to grow existing SME LAF and the need to consolidate it first.

risks_watch: Gross NPS rose to 1.13% from 0.95% QoQ; monitor whether SME stress and the 30% slower-selling wholesale exposure lead to further NPA build-up.
Recoveries depend on SARFAESI legal case resolution timelines, which management says are expected to improve but gave no figures for.
SME disbursement recovery in H2 FY27 is promised but not quantified; watch the next quarter's CEO-led update.
Wholesale growth depends on residential real estate demand; a slowdown could hit the portfolio's non-affordable segment.
Concentration in about 80-90 builders and 128 projects; a rise in exposure to any single borrower would increase risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on wholesale growth, funding headroom and the Q2 record disbursement, but cautious and somewhat defensive on SME asset quality, saying the recovery is still unproven and the new CEO's impact can only be judged next quarter. On real estate, management is reassuring but gives little hard data on the slower-selling portion of the book.
key_quotes: Our focus is on you can say affordable housing where even if there is no kind of any slackness and the projects are getting oversold 5 to 10 times, it's a kind of a drop lottery system that is prevalent here.
So, we completely stopped and most of these accounts, the NPAs have come up during the book for one period between 22 to 24 and in last 18 months, there is no NPAs, which has come in last 18 months.
So, as a company with the size we are in and it doesn't make any sense to open a new vertical.
But we are hopeful that the thing should be better and last two months have been the best two months of this financial year for SME and we are hopeful that post Diwali our numbers will be better.

adds.what: SME branch network rationalisation: relocation of sub-scale branches (Gujarat, Rajasthan rural); no net capacity addition stated

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; wholesale growth backed by Rs 210 crore undrawn limits and a Rs 300-400 crore pipeline, while SME retail recovery is only deferred to H2 FY27 with no quantified targets; Q2 AUM +16% YoY and NII +21% YoY, with management prioritising asset quality over growth.

mgmt.note: A new full-time SME CEO is in place; management promised a fuller review next quarter, with no specific growth plan stated yet.
